==Problem==
When a student multiplied the number <imath>66</imath> by the repeating decimal, 
<cmath>\underline{1}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b} \ \underline{a} \ \underline{b}\ldots=\underline{1}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}},</cmath> 
where <imath>a</imath> and <imath>b</imath> are digits, he did not notice the notation and just multiplied <imath>66</imath> times <imath>\underline{1}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}.</imath> Later he found that his answer is <imath>0.5</imath> less than the correct answer. What is the <imath>2</imath>-digit number <imath>\underline{a} \ \underline{b}?</imath>

<imath>\textbf{(A) }15 \qquad \textbf{(B) }30 \qquad \textbf{(C) }45 \qquad \textbf{(D) }60 \qquad \textbf{(E) }75</imath>

==Solution 1==
We are given that <imath>66\Bigl(\underline{1}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}\Bigr)-0.5=66\Bigl(\underline{1}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}\Bigr),</imath> from which
<cmath>\begin{align*}
66\Bigl(\underline{1}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}\Bigr)-66\Bigl(\underline{1}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}\Bigr)&=0.5 \\
66\Bigl(\underline{1}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}} - \underline{1}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}\Bigr)&=0.5 \\
66\Bigl(\underline{0}.\underline{0} \ \underline{0} \ \overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}\Bigr)&=0.5 \\
66\left(\frac{1}{100}\cdot\underline{0}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}\right)&=\frac12 \\
\underline{0}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}&=\frac{25}{33} \\
\underline{0}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}&=0.\overline{75} \\
\underline{a} \ \underline{b}&=\boxed{\textbf{(E) }75}.
\end{align*}</cmath>
~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 2==
It is known that <imath>\underline{0}.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}=\frac{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}{99}</imath> and <imath>\underline{0}.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}=\frac{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}{100}.</imath> 

Let <imath>x=\underline{a} \ \underline{b}.</imath> We have <cmath>66\biggl(1+\frac{x}{99}\biggr)-66\biggl(1+\frac{x}{100}\biggr)=0.5.</cmath> Expanding and simplifying give <imath>\frac{x}{150}=0.5,</imath> so <imath>x=\boxed{\textbf{(E) }75}.</imath> 

~aop2014 ~BakedPotato66 ~MRENTHUSIASM

==Solution 3 (Similar to Solution 2)==

We have <cmath>66 \cdot \left(1 + \frac{10a+b}{100}\right) + \frac{1}{2} = 66 \cdot \left(1+ \frac{10a+b}{99}\right).</cmath>
Expanding both sides, we have <cmath>66 + \frac{33(10a+b)}{50} + \frac{1}{2} = 66 + \frac{2(10a+b)}{3}.</cmath>
Subtracting <imath>66</imath> from both sides, we have <cmath>\frac{33(10a+b)}{50} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2(10a+b)}{3}.</cmath>
Multiplying both sides by <imath>50 \cdot 3 = 150,</imath> we have <cmath>99(10a+b) + 75 = 100(10a+b).</cmath>
Thus, the answer is <imath>10a+b = \boxed{\textbf{(E) }75}.</imath>

By letting <imath>x=\underline{a} \ \underline{b}=10a+b,</imath> this solution is similar to Solution 2. In this solution, we solve for <imath>10a+b</imath> as a whole.

==Solution 4 (Answer Choices & Modular) ==

Let <imath>\underline{a} \ \underline{b}</imath> represent the two-digit number <imath>ab</imath>, not the product of the digits <imath>a</imath> and <imath>b</imath>. We can construct fractions for the values <imath>1.\underline{a} \ \underline{b}</imath>, and <imath>1.\overline{\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}</imath>, which are <imath>\frac{1\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}{100}</imath> and <imath>\frac{1\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}{99}</imath>  respectively. Multiplying by <imath>66</imath> on both sides and adding <imath>1/2</imath> to <imath>\frac{1\underline{a} \ \underline{b}}{100}</imath> and simplifying, we get this: <cmath>\frac{33 * \underline{a}\underline{b} + 25}{50} = \frac{2\underline{a}\underline{b}}{3}.</cmath>

Looking at the answer choices, we notice that all of them are divisible by <imath>3</imath>. This means that since the right-hand side will result in an integer, the left-hand side needs to as well. This means that the numerator of the left-hand side fraction has to be divisible by <imath>50</imath>. So, we get this expression:

<imath>33 * \underline{a}\underline{b}\ + 25 \equiv 0\pmod{50}. </imath>

<imath>33 * \underline{a}\underline{b}\ \equiv -25\pmod{50}. </imath>

<imath>33 * \underline{a}\underline{b}\ \equiv 25\pmod{50}. </imath>

This means that the product of <imath>33</imath> and <imath>\underline{a}\underline{b}</imath> must have a remainder of <imath>25</imath> when divided by <imath>50</imath>. Since it must have a remainder of <imath>25</imath>, the product should have a units digit of <imath>5</imath>, which eliminates <imath>\textbf{(B) }</imath> and <imath>\textbf{(D) }</imath>. Multiplying <imath>33</imath> to the rest of the answer choices, the only one which fills this requirement is <imath>75</imath>, which is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(E) }75}.</imath>

~neeyakkid23
==Solution 5 (A different way to calculate)==

<imath>1.\overline{ab}=1+\dfrac{\overline{ab}_{10}}{10^2-1}=1+\dfrac{10a+b}{99}</imath> and <imath>1.ab=1+\dfrac{a}{10}+\dfrac{b}{100}</imath>, so our equation is 
<cmath>66\times\left(1+\dfrac{10a+b}{99}\right)=66\times\left(1+\dfrac{a}{10}+\dfrac{b}{100}\right)+0.5,</cmath>so now let's simplify!
\begin{align*}
66\times\left(1+\dfrac{10a+b}{99}\right)&=66\times\left(1+\dfrac{a}{10}+\dfrac{b}{100}\right)+0.5\\
1+\dfrac{10a+b}{99}&=1+\dfrac{a}{10}+\dfrac{b}{100}+\dfrac1{132}\\
\dfrac{10a+b}{99}&=\dfrac{10a+b}{100}+\dfrac1{132}.
\end{align*}
Notice that the <imath>2</imath>-digit number <imath>\overline{ab}</imath> is just <imath>10a+b</imath>. Therefore, let's just find the value of <imath>10a+b</imath>.
\newpage
\begin{align*}
\left(\dfrac1{99}-\dfrac1{100}\right)(10a+b)&=\dfrac1{132}\\
10a+b&=\dfrac{\dfrac1{132}}{\dfrac1{99}-\dfrac1{100}}\\
10a+b&=\dfrac{\dfrac1{132}}{\dfrac{100-99}{99\times100}}\\
10a+b&=\dfrac{9900}{132}\\
10a+b&=75.
\end{align*}
We just got <imath>10a+b=75</imath>, and <imath>75</imath> is indeed a <imath>2</imath>-digit number, so the two-digit number <imath>\overline{ab}</imath> is <imath>\boxed{75}</imath>.

~Yuhao2012
